This book follows the order in which a data science project meets its problems and not the order of a syllabus. Across a decade in energy, industrial and semiconductor settings, the failures that cost the most were seldom in the model. They were a problem that had not been stated precisely, a pipeline that nobody could rerun, and a system that drifted unnoticed after it went live. The sequence of the book, from Python and data analysis through classical machine learning to monitoring and value, answers those failures in the order in which they occur.

The reader in mind is an early-career data scientist or engineer who is moving from notebooks to systems that other people depend on. Each chapter is therefore a notebook that runs, because a concept that cannot be run is difficult to check, and the examples draw on energy and supply chain data, where much of this was learned.

More of the work behind the book is at [sambaiga.github.io](https://sambaiga.github.io).
